claims.statement: app/globals.css is the single runtime style entrypoint: it imports Tailwind v4 and the layout-only app/design-system.css, then defines the :root token block copied verbatim from docs/design/colors_and_type.css, which the file's own header designates the source of truth for color; app/design-system.css contains only layout/component classes (shell, sidebar, topbar, buttons, focus, data rows, keyframes) that reference token variables, and tremor chart utilities are bridged via @config scoped to the analytics module.

IBM Plex Sans (300-600) and IBM Plex Mono (300-500) are self-hosted with next/font in app/layout.tsx, exposing --font-ibm-plex-sans/--font-ibm-plex-mono on <html>, and :root in app/globals.css prepends those variables to --font-sans/--font-mono so the optimized layout-shift-free fonts win with system names as fallbacks; Inter/Geist/Roboto/Arial are banned as primary typefaces.

The color system is six semantic hues (blue informational/TWSP, teal CFSP, green completed/approved/on-track, amber warning 7-21 days, red critical <7 days/errors, purple NC levels) with staged tokens per hue (base/-lt/-dk/-border/-hover; purple defines base/-lt/-dk), and every color carries exactly one meaning; the urgency tier (critical <=6 days, warning 7-21, on-track >21) is the pure domain function urgencyTier() applied to daysToBilling, which is computed once at data fetch and stored on the batch - daysUntil() returns Infinity for a missing or unparseable deadline so absent dates never trigger urgency tiers.

Documented deviations (marked in DESIGN.md, which win over the spec): amber and red hex values were re-tinted warmer/more vivid, and the spec's 3px colored left border was removed from BatchCards, InfoCallouts (now a 1px tinted full-perimeter border), and warning/critical MetricCards (now a tinted label icon and sub-label), with urgency instead communicated by the header badge and the billing-deadline value color.

The primary icon system, shared/ui/Icon.tsx, renders an inline map of Tabler 2px-stroke SVG path strings with currentColor inheritance and aria-hidden, ported verbatim from the design handoff to keep glyphs pixel-identical and avoid a runtime dependency; it is pure render and safe in both Server and Client trees. @tabler/icons-react is declared in package.json as the spec-canonical library, and the only current direct importer is modules/auth/ui/SignUpModal.tsx.

No emoji are allowed anywhere in the UI (and no Unicode glyph or PNG icons); UI copy follows the administrative voice rules: no exclamation marks, no we/you, Title Case for data-system nouns (Batch, Scholar, NTP, BSRS, NC II), sentence case for buttons/labels, and units always included with numbers.

Status is conveyed by text plus icon, never color alone, targeting WCAG 2.2 AA (the upstream spec sheet states WCAG 2.1 AA; the repo rule is the stricter target). This is enforced structurally: the focus-visible ring (2px blue, 2px offset) was added because the ported stylesheet had no focus rule at all, and billing-queue row selection is announced structurally via aria-selected, never by tint alone.

Component layering is app route Server Component -> modules/<domain>/ui screens -> shared/ui props-only primitives: routes are thin (fetch via a module's data/, compose module UI), another module's data/ is private with only app/ able to fetch it, shared/ can never import modules/ or app/, and raw DB types from lib/supabase/database.types.ts are restricted to data layers - all enforced by import/no-restricted-paths in eslint.config.mjs. If a shared/ui component starts reading data or encoding business rules, it must be moved into its owning module.

Components default to Server Components with client islands only for interactivity: BatchCard is 'use client' for hover elevation and opening BatchModal, Sidebar is 'use client' for pathname/drawer/tenant state, while the dashboard layout and page are Server Components.

Existing primitives (BatchCard, BatchModal, StatusBadge, LifecyclePipeline, EmptyState, InfoCallout, etc.) must be reused rather than creating parallels; CardsView and TableView both compose the same BatchCard/BatchModal/StatusBadge/EmptyState set, differing only in arrangement.

Every data screen must implement all six mandatory states - loading, empty, no-results, error/sync-failed, permission-denied, stale-data - and screens with relative dates must show an exact 'Data as of' timestamp (RULES.md section 4, rule 24).

Data screens derive their view from four-state discriminated snapshots: getBatchesSnapshot() (React cache-wrapped so layout and page share one query) yields BatchesSnapshot of ok (rows plus dataAsOf from the freshest updated_at) / sync-failed / unconfigured, while no-tenant-access is folded in by routes via withTenantAccess rather than produced by the query. selectBatchesForDisplay never substitutes mock data - any non-ok snapshot renders an honest empty or failure state (shared/mocks was removed entirely in the mock-data retirement, and RULES 3.19 bans fabricated data) - and sync-failed must surface the failure with the full-page retry guard checked before the empty guard. The dashboard additionally supports ?state= preview overrides: denied is preview-only until the tenant/role resolver (TES-34 / issue #32), and stale is real data freshness - the freshest row's updated_at older than the 24h DATA_STALE_AFTER_MS threshold.

The 'Data as of' stamp is formatted from the freshest live updated_at as e.g. 'Jun 19, 2026 . 14:02' using hourCycle h23 (midnight prints 00:02, never 24:02); a stamp only exists on an ok snapshot, so DashboardHeader degrades to the literal word 'unknown' instead of printing a fake precise timestamp and renders staleness as a text STALE badge beside the stamp, never color alone. BillingQueueView receives its dataAsOf as an explicit prop stamped as 'Packet readiness . Data as of {dataAsOf}' with a ' . STALE' suffix when stale.
UI copy must never imply official TESDA approval or submission: the app is an internal working layer and TESDA SIS/T2MIS/BSRS remain authoritative (RULES.md section 5, rule 27).

assets/, preview/, screenshots/, ui_kits/, and uploads/ are ported verbatim from the design bundle and excluded from lint (eslint globalIgnores, which also ignores vendored .claude/** and .agents/** tooling); the PreToolUse hook script .claude/hooks/protect-static-dirs.sh blocks agent Edit/Write under those directories, exiting 2 with the instruction to edit the source design files first, and public/assets/ is explicitly exempt as the app's real runtime static directory. The registration file .claude/settings.json is gitignored by design (.claude/* with selective re-includes for hooks/, agents/, skills/) and absent from the checkout, so hook registration is per-machine local configuration - the version-controlled artifacts are the hook scripts and the [hook]/[deny] declarations in RULES.md. FIGMA FILES/, diagrams/, and .design-sync/ are review-level design artifacts, and FIGMA FILES/ and .design-sync/ are not currently materialized in the tree - Figma pages are referenced by node ID in code comments.

The design-sync workflow makes the local Next.js TypeScript components the implementation layer and the handoff bundle the design reference (ui_kits/admin/*.jsx are the prototype components the local ones were ported from, and ui_kits/admin/index.html is the working no-build prototype); when spec and deviation conflict the deviation wins and colors_and_type.css plus ui_kits/admin/ are the live ground truth, so design changes go to the source design files first.

The shell MetricsRow enforces compliance-copy invariants against false alarms: the hasBatches guard is load-bearing (TES-74) so an empty batch set is never styled as a critical red billing deadline, and 'All verified' must not appear when there is nothing to verify (unknown, not cleared, per ADR-004).

no-tenant-access is a fact about membership, not about data: a profile with zero tenant memberships reads zero rows from every RLS-scoped table as a successful empty read, so routes fold the tenancy verdict (granted/none/unknown) into the snapshot via withTenantAccess (modules/tenancy/domain/access), which replaces only an ok snapshot and treats unknown as no-rewrite; data screens render shared/ui/NoTenantAccessState ('No school assigned yet', one shared copy across screens) and must check it before the ordinary empty guard.

The (dashboard) Server Component layout resolves role surfaces before rendering: isAdmin from the trusted profile role (never the ?role= preview) drives the admin-only 'Add user' nav row, and the ADR-006 platform-admin axis is resolved separately through the boolean-only isPlatformAdmin() helper over the security-definer RPC current_user_is_platform_admin (the platform_admins table is unreadable through the anon client), so any failure hides the 'Add school' row rather than rendering a link into a denial; the MetricsRow is omitted entirely on sync-failed or no-tenant-access so a zero-metrics strip is never shown as a claim about a school.

The dashboard route fails closed on identity: a trusted-role lookup that itself errors (lookup-failed) renders a dedicated 'Couldn't verify your access' EmptyState with Retry instead of defaulting to a permissive role, and a trusted trainer role redirects to /trainer before any data loads; ?role= may only pick the displayed office-role variant (coordinator/admin/viewer, least-privilege viewer fallback via toOfficeRole), never the redirect.

The dashboard ships a route-level app/(dashboard)/dashboard/loading.tsx Suspense boundary whose token-based shimmer skeleton mirrors the real layout (header, KPI row, charts row, panels) under aria-busy, and write-back controls show the width-stable .btn.loading leading-slot spinner with aria-busy (slowed to 2s under prefers-reduced-motion).
